title: Orchard and Vow Anew
premise: Rafael Nystrom, a marine biologist retreating to her late grandmother's coastal orchard after a devastating breakup, discovers the deed lists a second name: Elias Thorne, the boy who left her fifteen years ago and now returns as co-inheritor. Forced to share one harvest season on land neither can afford alone, they rebuild trust through grafting trees, storm repairs, and the town's meddling warmth, while Rafael's research grant and Elias's city obligations pull them apart. When a developer's offer threatens the orchard and Rafael must choose between her career posting abroad and the life growing here, she finally lets someone stay past the last train. The story ends with the two signing the deed jointly as partners in both senses, planting a new orchard row as the first autumn leaves fall.
about_author: Silas Yarrow is the pen name of a former agricultural extension agent who spent a decade cataloguing heirloom fruit varieties along the northern coast before turning to fiction. Their novels braid rural labor, family inheritance, and second-chance romance with an unflinching tenderness for stubborn places and stubborn people.

chapters.title: The Deed in the Tin Box
chapters.summary: Rafael arrives at her grandmother's neglected orchard to settle the estate and finds the deed naming two owners: herself and Elias Thorne. Her POV; grief curdles into disbelief as she recognizes the name she swore she'd buried. Emotional beat: shock and defensive anger.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Flashback-tinged chapter establishing Rafael's research posting offer in Costa Rica and the breakup that made her flee fieldwork for paperwork. Her POV; she rationalizes that she'll sell fast and leave. Beat: avoidance dressed up as practicality.

chapters.title: A Truck at the Gate
chapters.summary: Elias arrives unannounced, older, guarded, holding his own copy of the deed. His POV reveals he learned of the inheritance only weeks ago and suspects their grandmothers schemed deliberately. Beat: wary hostility masking old wounds.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: The two draft a hostile agreement: split costs, sell by season's end, no personal questions. Alternating POV; lawyerly distance barely conceals charged history. Beat: brittle truce.

chapters.title: What the Storm Took
chapters.summary: A night storm fells the oldest pear row and floods the root cellar. They work side by side until dawn. Rafael's POV; muscle memory of teamwork she thought forgotten. Beat: reluctant intimacy through shared labor.

chapters.title: The Town That Remembers
chapters.summary: At the general store, neighbors greet Elias like a returning son and Rafael like a ghost, revealing how each was talked about after he left. Dual POV. Beat: the weight of communal memory and belonging neither chose.

chapters.title: Grafting Season
chapters.summary: Elias, it turns out, apprenticed under Rafael's grandmother; he teaches Rafael to graft scions onto hardy rootstock. Her POV; watching his hands, she remembers being seventeen. Beat: tenderness breaking through resentment.

chapters.title: The Developer's Letter
chapters.summary: An offer arrives: a resort chain wants the waterfront parcel at a price that would solve everything. Elias is tempted; Rafael recoils. His POV. Beat: first real conflict of values.

chapters.title: Tide Charts and Train Schedules
chapters.summary: Rafael's grant deadline looms; she maps escape routes while pretending not to. Her POV interwoven with Elias noticing her packed boxes. Beat: quiet dread of another departure.

chapters.title: The Reason He Left
chapters.summary: Marta, the town postmistress, forces out the truth: Elias left because his father's debts endangered the Thornes' farm, and he took the blame for something Rafael's uncle did. His POV. Beat: reframing fifteen years of abandonment.

chapters.title: She Doesn't Ask
chapters.summary: Rafael learns fragments of the truth from Marta but refuses to confront Elias, retreating into turtle survey data at the estuary. Her POV. Beat: self-protection as slow self-harm.

chapters.title: Bees in the Blossom
chapters.summary: Spring bloom; hired hands arrive, and the orchard hums with life. A festival planning committee ropes them both in. Dual POV. Beat: accidental domesticity, laughter returning.

chapters.title: The Kiss at the Cider Press
chapters.summary: After a long pressing day, flour-dusted and exhausted, they kiss in the press house—and Rafael immediately retreats. Her POV. Beat: desire colliding with terror of loss.

chapters.title: Cold Storage
chapters.summary: A week of pointed politeness; Elias signs the developer's letter of intent 'pending inspection,' a move Rafael reads as betrayal. His POV shows he did it to force a decision before she vanishes. Beat: misread motives, widening rift.

chapters.title: The Estuary Survey
chapters.summary: Rafael throws herself into tagging turtles; Elias shows up to help haul nets, wordless. Her POV. Beat: apology without words, fragile thaw.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Letters
chapters.summary: In the attic they find years of correspondence between the two grandmothers—evidence the co-deed was deliberate matchmaking across decades. Alternating POV. Beat: wonder, then anger at being managed.

chapters.title: The Uncle Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Rafael's uncle Dean appears, charming, angling for a cut of the sale and dropping hints about Elias's father's ruin. Her POV. Beat: protective fury on Elias's behalf she doesn't yet understand.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Packing Shed
chapters.summary: Dean's insinuations detonate; Rafael demands the whole truth from Elias. He gives it: the debt, the sacrifice, the silence. His POV. Beat: catharsis and raw exposure.

chapters.title: Rain on Tin Roofs
chapters.summary: They spend a storm-bound day indoors talking for the first time like adults—griefs, failures, the people they became apart. Dual POV. Beat: honest reckoning, love re-entering the room.

chapters.title: Blossom Festival
chapters.summary: The town festival crowns them, half-jokingly, the orchard's stewards; dancing under string lights, they nearly say it aloud. Rafael's POV. Beat: joy with an expiration date she keeps checking.

chapters.title: The Offer from the South
chapters.summary: Costa Rica confirms: Rafael's dream posting, starting in six weeks, non-negotiable. Her POV. Beat: the future she wanted reasserting itself at the worst moment.

chapters.title: He Signs Nothing
chapters.summary: Elias quietly withdraws from the developer deal, betting the orchard's solvency on a cider venture. His POV. Beat: faith in a future he can't make her share.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies of Omission
chapters.summary: Rafael discovers the withdrawn contract and feels deceived all over again; they fight about who gets to sacrifice for whom. Alternating POV. Beat: love weaponized into pride.

chapters.title: The Empty Side of the Bed
chapters.summary: After a reconciling night, Rafael wakes early and packs, unable to bear choosing. Her POV. Beat: shame and flight instinct.

chapters.title: Last Train North
chapters.summary: She stands at the platform; the train comes; she watches it leave without boarding—but tells Elias she almost didn't come back. His POV. Beat: the blurb's promise inverted—she stays, but honesty lags behind.

chapters.title: Summer Fruit
chapters.summary: First harvest together; the cider venture's debut at market succeeds beyond hope. Dual POV. Beat: earned sweetness, brief peace.

chapters.title: Dean's Paper Trail
chapters.summary: Dean contests the will, claiming undue influence by the grandmothers, threatening both inheritances. Rafael's POV. Beat: external threat crystallizing stakes.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Courtroom testimony forces both to declare what the orchard means; Elias publicly chooses Rafael over his own claim. His POV. Beat: love stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: What She Almost Said
chapters.summary: Despite victory, Rafael withdraws—she hasn't declined Costa Rica, and guilt makes her cruel. Her POV. Beat: sabotage from within.

chapters.title: The Row We Didn't Plant
chapters.summary: Elias plants the new orchard row alone, leaving one gap. His POV. Beat: heartbreak rendered in horticulture.

chapters.title: Marta's Intervention
chapters.summary: Marta gives Rafael the final grandmother letter: 'Love isn't staying put, girl—it's letting someone stay.' Her POV. Beat: the thematic key turned.

chapters.title: Declining the Sea
chapters.summary: Rafael calls Costa Rica and declines—not abandoning science but negotiating a coastal research station based here. Her POV. Beat: refusing the false binary between duty and love.

chapters.title: The Gap in the Row
chapters.summary: She finds Elias at dawn filling the empty gap with a sapling they grafted together. Wordless reconciliation. Alternating POV. Beat: forgiveness made physical.

chapters.title: The Developer Returns
chapters.summary: The resort escalates: a hostile bid to the county, zoning hearing scheduled. Dual POV. Beat: climax approaching, town mobilizes.

chapters.title: Standing Room Only
chapters.summary: The zoning hearing; the town testifies, Rafael presents the estuary's protected habitat data, Elias presents the orchard's living history. Beat: collective courage.

chapters.title: Vow Anew
chapters.summary: The bid dies; walking home through the orchard at dusk, they exchange vows—not wedding vows, but promises to stay, to tell the truth, to plant what outlives them. Dual POV. Beat: emotional climax.

chapters.title: Signing Day
chapters.summary: They sign the deed jointly, add a codicil protecting the land in perpetuity, and celebrate with the first bottled cider. Alternating POV. Beat: resolution of inheritance theme.

chapters.title: The Station on the Point
chapters.summary: Months later: Rafael's research station opens; turtles tagged, students taught, Elias running the cidery beside it. Her POV. Beat: integration of every thread.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: Autumn's first frost; they harvest the last fruit and walk the new row, now budding. His POV. Beat: quiet gratitude, cycles renewed.

chapters.title: Orchard and Vow
chapters.summary: Epilogue: a spring morning years later, a child helps them graft new scions; the letters from the grandmothers rest framed in the press house. Dual POV closing. Beat: belonging inherited forward—love as the truest deed.
